paragraphs.text: Good evening, sisters and elders. I'm sorry to be so late today with the podcast. I have really enjoyed zone interviews again today. We have such great missionaries in this mission. Excellent teachers, kind and wonderful people. I'm seeing so many acts of patience, tolerance, kindness in the mission right now that it's just inspiring to me. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you for being the kind of people that you are. I'm truly grateful to serve with you.

Our transfer day was supposed to be tomorrow, but with the lockdown, the area presidency has instructed the mission presidents to not do any transferring of missionaries until the rules become quite a bit less strict. The police and the army personnel seem to be getting more strict than before and probably a little more easily irritated. And I think that's probably due to some people just not respecting the rules. We don't want to add to the stress of the situation. So we're going to do our best to comply with every instruction.

Now, tomorrow on the podcast, I'm going to talk you through a progressive muscle relaxation meditation. It may seem a little strange for some of you, but I want to assure you that it really works to relax your body and your mind. You can use it before bed or you can use it in the morning. I'll usually use it a couple of times a day.

The one that I'm going to share with you tomorrow will have a few words said at the end, which are designed to clear your head and bring your energy back up so that you can use it in the morning. If you want to use it before bed, just skip that last few words that I share and you'll drift right off to sleep. So anyway, I want to share that with you. It's kind of an experiment and you can tell me whether or not it's useful to you. But that's tomorrow's podcast and I'll upload it by about eight o'clock so you can try it in the morning.

Tonight, I want to just share a few thoughts with you on revelation. Many of you have asked me in these interviews, both this time and last time, how you can know when the Spirit is prompting you versus your own ideas, how you can get more inspiration, how you can really tap into the Spirit of Revelation a little better. Those are great questions and I honor and respect you for asking them because it's the sort of thing that you need to be asking about at this season in your life.

But let's start with a scripture that teaches a great principle here. This is found in the Old Testament. It's in 1 Kings chapter 19 verses 11 through 13. You probably have heard this scripture before, but I think we should just listen to it again and ponder it a little bit, quote, "And, behold, the Lord passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the Lord; but the Lord was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the Lord was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the Lord was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice. And it was so, when Elijah heard it," close quote. Again, that was 1 Kings 19:11–13.

The key element of that passage of scripture is the concept that you can have a lot of really dramatic things going on around you. Earthquakes and tempests and typhoons and fires and all the other things going on, a lot of noise, but that's not how the Lord's going to communicate with you. The words describing his communication are still and small.

Elder Dallin H. Oaks said this, quote, "Visions do happen. Voices are heard from beyond the veil. I know this, but these experiences are exceptional. Most of the revelation that comes to leaders and members of the Church comes by the still, small voice or by a feeling rather than by a vision or a voice that speaks specific words we can hear. I can testify to the reality of that kind of revelation, which I have come to know as a familiar, even daily experience to guide me in the work of the Lord," close quote.

As Elder Oaks points out here, even to apostles, most of the time, and I would say that their daily experience of being guided by the Spirit is just about the same as our experience being guided by the Spirit. Learning how to listen to the still small voice is really learning how to listen to righteous feelings.

Let's hear now from President Boyd K. Packer, also a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, quote, "These delicate, refined spiritual communications are not seen with our eyes nor heard with our ears. And even though it is described as a voice, it is a voice that one feels more than one hears," close quote.

As we think about this, I think all of us can point to experiences where we've had a feeling. It wasn't a voice or a thing that we saw. We just had a feeling, but the clarity around the feeling seemed to cause it to be like something we heard or something we saw.

I think this can be explained by realizing that a spirit to spirit communication is going to be a powerful communication. And the more we are tuned into it, the more it's going to feel like the kind of communication we're used to on this part of our mortal probation.

Elder Tamayo shared something earlier today in the MLC chat where he talked about us being not physical beings having a spiritual experience, but spiritual beings having a physical experience. And truly, that is the situation. But while we're having this physical experience, it's so physical and it's so constant, we can sometimes forget that the really deep communication is spiritual. And so we'll try to define it with the words that we use to define the physical experience.

But let's read a couple more scriptures. This is from Doctrine and Covenants section 11 verses 12 and 13. "And now, verily, verily, I say unto thee, put your trust in that Spirit which leadeth to do good—yea, to do justly, to walk humbly, to judge righteously; and this is my Spirit. Verily, verily, I say unto you, I will impart unto you of my Spirit, which shall enlighten your mind, which shall fill your soul with joy;"

As we look at that, we begin to realize, well, now this is interesting. When we have these feelings to apologize, to forgive, to repent, to say a kind word, to do a kind deed, when we have these feelings to maybe not say the harsh thing that we were going to say, or to go mend this relationship that we've damaged in a previous interaction, those are very real revelations.

Now, we resist them because the natural man, which all of us have way too much of, doesn't want to yield to the enticements of the Holy Spirit. But as we do, we find yielding brings us peace, it brings us joy, and that's how we can know that we're being guided by the Spirit.

So, just as a conclusion to this short podcast, I want you to experiment tomorrow. I want you to think every time you have the idea or the impression or the thought or the feeling that you ought to do something nice to someone else, something kind, and then you do it. Notice how you feel afterwards.

The feeling you have after you do something is a better way for you to know about its effect, whether it was from God or whether it was from some other source, than any other thing. Now, this is not a fail-safe way that you should figure everything out, but we make enough mistakes in our lives, we make enough good choices in our lives that we can look back upon those experiences and say, wow, I didn't like the way I felt after I did that. That did not make me feel peace. That left me unsettled. There's a good clue that that wasn't from the Lord.

On the other hand, when we've done something good and we have those feelings, we feel settled. We feel comfortable. We feel peace. We can look at that and say, that's interesting. Look how I felt after I did that thing. Now, this is a lot, I think this is a lot what Joseph Smith was trying to teach us when he talked about growing into the spirit of revelation.

When we grow into the spirit of revelation, it's all about studying how we feel after we've acted on some idea, thought, or impression we've had. And as we begin to make a distinction between those things that uplift and edify us, that bring us joy, and those things that unsettle us and make us irritated and uncomfortable and defensive and argumentative, we can clearly see this gap, this division between those things that come from the natural man and those things that come from the spirit of God.

I hope you find this useful. The number one thing I want you to get out of this short podcast, though, is that it's important for you to reflect upon the things that you do and how you feel after you do them. As you do that, you will find yourself growing into the spirit of revelation. Good night. Hope you sleep well. We'll talk to you in the morning.
